facts.fact_text: Immediately after the announcement of the preliminary results of the 19 February 2008 Armenian presidential election, Mr Levon Ter-Petrosyan called on his supporters to gather at Freedom Square in central Yerevan in order to protest against alleged irregularities in the election process.
From 20 February 2008 onwards, nationwide daily protest rallies were held by Mr Levon Ter-Petrosyan's supporters.
The main meeting place of Mr Levon Ter-Petrosyan's supporters during the post-election protest rallies was Freedom Square and the surrounding park in Yerevan.
The applicant was actively involved in the post-election protests following the 19 February 2008 Armenian presidential election.
The applicant regularly attended the demonstrations held at Freedom Square in Yerevan.
The applicant gave speeches at the demonstrations held at Freedom Square in Yerevan.
On 1 March 2008, at some point around 6-7 a.m., a police operation was conducted at Freedom Square in Yerevan where several hundred demonstrators were camping.
The applicant alleged that the aim of the police operation on 1 March 2008 at Freedom Square had been forcibly to terminate the assembly.
The applicant alleged that a large police force had violently attacked the demonstrators at Freedom Square with rubber batons and electric shock devices, without any prior warning.
The applicant alleged that the police attack on demonstrators at Freedom Square on 1 March 2008 forced the demonstrators to flee the square.
On 1 March 2008 a criminal case was instituted under several Articles of the Armenian Criminal Code in connection with the events at Freedom Square.
The criminal case instituted on 1 March 2008 in connection with the events at Freedom Square included charges of organising and holding an unlawful assembly.
The criminal case instituted on 1 March 2008 in connection with the events at Freedom Square included charges of incitement to disobedience of police orders to terminate the unlawful assembly.
The criminal case instituted on 1 March 2008 in connection with the events at Freedom Square included charges of illegal possession of arms and ammunition.
The criminal case instituted on 1 March 2008 in connection with the events at Freedom Square included charges of life-threatening assaults on police officers.
On 10 March 2008 the applicant was arrested by officers of the National Security Service on suspicion of usurpation of State power.
On 12 March 2008 the applicant was charged under Article 225 § 3 of the Armenian Criminal Code within the scope of criminal case no. 62202608.
On 12 March 2008 the applicant was charged under Article 300 § 1 of the Armenian Criminal Code (usurpation of State power) within the scope of criminal case no. 62202608.
The criminal case instituted on 1 March 2008 in connection with the events at Freedom Square included charges of organising and holding an unlawful assembly.
The criminal case instituted on 1 March 2008 in connection with the events at Freedom Square included charges of incitement to disobedience of police orders to terminate the unlawful assembly.
The criminal case instituted on 1 March 2008 in connection with the events at Freedom Square included charges of illegal possession of arms and ammunition.

The decision to institute criminal proceedings on 1 March 2008 stated that on 1 March 2008 at around 6 a.m., when the police took measures aimed at forcibly ending the public events held in violation of the procedure prescribed by law in compliance with the requirements of section 14 of the Assemblies, Rallies, Marches and Demonstrations Act, the organisers and participants committed a life- and health-threatening assault on police officers with clubs, metal rods and other adapted objects.
The Government alleged that the applicant and the group of opposition supporters whom he had joined had conspired to usurp State power.
The Government alleged that the assembly at Freedom Square had pursued the aim of usurping State power by discrediting the presidential election.
The Government alleged that the assembly at Freedom Square had pursued the aim of usurping State power by creating illusions of public discontent and revolt.
The Government alleged that the assembly at Freedom Square had pursued the aim of usurping State power by destabilising the internal political situation.

The Government claimed that the reason for the police operation at Freedom Square on 1 March 2008 had been to verify information obtained on the previous day by the Armenian Police and National Security Service, according to which a large number of weapons were to be distributed to the protesters to incite provocative actions and riots in Yerevan on 1 March 2008.
The applicant alleged that a large police force had violently attacked the demonstrators at Freedom Square with rubber batons and electric shock devices, without any prior warning.
The applicant alleged that the police attack on demonstrators at Freedom Square on 1 March 2008 forced the demonstrators to flee the square.

The Government alleged that the disorder which took place in Yerevan on 1 and 2 March 2008 had been incited and organised by the applicant in conspiracy with several other active opposition supporters.
The applicant contested the Government's allegation that the disorder which took place in Yerevan on 1 and 2 March 2008 had been incited and organised by the applicant.

In its Resolutions regarding the 19 February 2008 Armenian presidential election and the events that followed, the Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe (PACE) condemned the arrest and continuing detention of scores of persons, including more than 100 opposition supporters and three members of parliament.

The Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe (PACE) condemned the arrest and continuing detention of persons on seemingly artificial and politically motivated charges, especially those under Articles 225 and 300 of the Armenian Criminal Code.
